**Matched standby refusals now perform zero process observations/ps launches.** The native HTTP path skips ordinary pane provenance; the new service brake runs before `verify_native_host`. It uses a registry PK read plus schema guard and the receiver lease/precedence maps in memory, not OS liveness or tmux. A matching held claim returns immediately. The zero-read regression actually executes; existing takeover cases still exercise the full proof when the brake does not match.

This also skips the later dead-owner/full-registry and admission work for that refused attempt. Conversely, candidates that do not match the brake pay one additional PK lookup and then retain the normal proof. Missing/lapsed/different-incarnation holders do not become proof-free admissions: the brake only refuses.

**Extension rate/scaling:** after three consecutive holder refusals, the existing standby timer changes from30s to600s. In an otherwise unchanged standby this is **2 timed retries/min to0.1/min per waiting session**, a20x reduction; aggregate cost scales with standby sessions/waiters, not merely the number of registered seats. Its own new prompt/live resume cancels the wait and re-arms; successful registration clears the refusal count. Cleanup aborts the old delay and removes its waiter, rather than accumulating timers. History-only resume events do not re-arm.

The ten-minute check remains0 ps **while the holder still keeps the seat**. A real takeover goes through normal host proof and may launch its expected ps; that is not a standby-refusal cost regression. Old precedence-reporting extensions benefit from the daemon brake without reloading; the extension update additionally reduces request volume.

**Not zero CPU/store work:** the startup retry still fetches the local roster before registering; that read projects registry/status/roles. Initial host inspection is outside the standby loop. The early brake's PK/schema read and in-memory lease checks also remain on old extensions' frequent retries. Thus a bounce can remove the measured lease-ps source, but need not erase all daemon CPU. The observed8 ps/min per named holder is an aggregate measurement; the30s timer's rate is per standby context.
